title: Canotto bake
description: One logged bake. It carries its own copy of the dough and protocol, so a bake stays truthful about what was actually made even after the recipe it came from is edited.

bakedAt.description: When the first pizza went on the deck. Local time, not necessarily with a zone.

recipeId.description: The recipe this run came from, if it still exists.

planned.description: True for a bake queued but not yet made. Planned bakes are excluded from analysis.

issues.description: Fault identifiers from the troubleshooting list, such as gumline or rim-dense.

equipment.description: What it was made and baked with.

ovenId.description: Oven type: gas-portable, gas-deck, wood, electric-pizza, home-steel or custom.

mixerId.description: Mixer type: hand, spiral, planetary, fork, processor or custom. Sets the friction allowance.

actuals.description: Measured on the day, as opposed to planned. Null where it was not recorded. Temperatures in degrees Celsius.

ambientTempC.description: Air temperature where the baking happened. Matters most for outdoor ovens.

fdtC.description: Final dough temperature at the end of the mix.

fridgeTempC.description: Measured, which is often not what the dial says.

coreTempC.description: Core of the ball at launch.

scores.description: One to five, or null where not judged. The overall score is the mean of whichever were given.

doneAt.title: Recorded times
doneAt.description: When each protocol step was actually checked off, as milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Absolute instants, never the gaps between them, so any one of them can be corrected without moving the rest. Keys are step ids from the protocol schema. Only the steps that bound a phase are recorded: p1-3 and p1-4 bound the biga's ambient rest, p1-4 and p2-1 the biga's cold hold, p2-1 and p4-1 the mix and bench, p4-1 and p5-1 the cold proof, p5-1 and p5-4 the counter temper. A phase with both bounds present ran for the difference between them; a phase with neither ran for whatever the schedule says. Consumers judging a bake should prefer these durations over the planned ones.
